sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Development server and forwarding setup
sections.what: Sets up the local development server: the React plugin, the src shortcut, the port, and the forwarding of /api calls to the backend.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the local app call the backend without cross-site problems.
sections.watch_out: The forwarding must match the rule in vercel.json, or local and live behavior will differ.

summary: Configures the Vite development server and build: the React plugin, a short name for the src folder, the dev port, and forwarding of /api requests to the backend during development.
purpose: Controls how the app runs on a developer's machine.
why: Likely reason: the development server has no backend of its own, so /api requests are forwarded to the backend to avoid cross-site problems.
how: It loads the React plugin, maps the @ shortcut to the src folder, and sets the port from the VITE_PORT setting or uses 5173. It forwards /api to the backend address from VITE_API_URL or to localhost port 8000, removing the /api prefix.
inputs: The environment settings VITE_PORT and VITE_API_URL, if they are set.
outputs: A running development server on the chosen port, with API calls forwarded to the backend.
risks: The forwarding only applies in development. Production uses the separate forwarding in vercel.json, so the two must stay in sync. The @ shortcut is defined, but the code shown uses relative imports, so it may be unused.
debug: If API calls fail during development, check VITE_API_URL and whether the backend runs on the target port. If the port is in use, set VITE_PORT.
